newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach drops on regulatory fears.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach drops on regulatory fears.

text.p: Stagecoach Holdings Plc shares fell on Wednesday amid fears that the bus and train group will be subject to a tough regulatory squeeze if Labour, as expected, wins the forthcoming election, dealers said.
Stagecoach shares were down 28-1/2 at 695 by 1136 GMT in volume of 1.1 million shares.
A report in the Independent newspaper highlighted the Labour threat to the company after the cancellation of a scheduled grilling by legislators of executives from its South West Trains (SWT) unit.
"Presuming Labour does sweep to power, SWT may be in for a rougher ride than anything the select committee could throw at it," the report said.
SWT has come under fire in recent weeks for cancelling trains after making a large number of drivers redundant. It is already being fined for underperformance by the industry regulator.

Separately Labour's economics spokesman Gordon Brown on Tuesday repeated his plan to impose a windfall tax on privatised utilities and dealers said there were concerns this could include companies like Stagecoach.
Yesterday Labour indicated that British Telecommunciations Plc and airport operator BAA Plc could fall within the scope of the tax.
Earlier this month, Labour transport spokesman Andrew Smith pledged a regulatory clampdown on the rail industry in an interview with Reuters.
Smith cited rail franchise operators and Railtrack Plc as the most likely targets of a tougher approach and said cancellations by SWT were an example of regulatory weakness.

By 1158 GMT, Stagecoach shares were down 36p at 687-1/2 in volume of 1.1 million shares. The stock surged to a record 803p on January 22 on the back of enthusiasm for the company's acquisition of train leasing group Porterbrook.
